purpose: Lapatinib is used to treat a certain type of breast cancer that has spread to other parts of the body. It is specifically for breast cancers that make too much of a protein called HER2. It is usually used together with another cancer medicine called capecitabine or letrozole.
how_it_works: Your cancer cells have proteins on their surface called HER2 and EGFR that act like on-switches, telling cancer cells to grow and divide. Lapatinib works by blocking these switches so the cancer cells cannot get the signal to keep growing. Think of it like putting a lock on the switch so it stays turned off.
common_side_effects: Diarrhea (very common and can be severe), nausea, vomiting, rash or dry skin, mouth sores, tiredness, loss of appetite, and redness or soreness on the palms of your hands or soles of your feet.
warnings: Lapatinib can cause serious heart problems, including a decrease in how well your heart pumps. It can also cause severe diarrhea that may lead to dehydration, so contact your doctor right away if diarrhea becomes bad. It may cause liver damage, so your liver will be monitored regularly. It can harm an unborn baby, so do not become pregnant while taking this medicine. It also interacts with many other medications, so always tell your doctor and pharmacist everything you are taking.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 1,250 mg (five 250 mg tablets) taken once a day on an empty stomach, at least one hour before or one hour after eating. Take all five tablets at the same time each day. Do not split or crush the tablets. If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regular time the following day — never double up.
